1: /**
2:  * The signal model: what a card contributes to a deck's plan, and in what
3:  * capacity.
4:  *
5:  * This replaces the old flat "theme" model, in which a signal was a single
6:  * regex applied identically to your card and to the candidate commander, and
7:  * two cards "synergised" when the same words appeared in both. That measured
8:  * lexical co-occurrence rather than synergy: "Sacrifice a creature" and
9:  * "Sacrifice Arid Mesa" are the same word and completely different mechanics,
10:  * and a commander that pays off a plan (Craterhoof Behemoth pumping your
11:  * board) usually shares no vocabulary at all with the cards that set it up.
12:  *
13:  * Three ideas do the work here.
14:  *
15:  * 1. ROLES. A card doesn't just "have" a theme, it participates in one in a
16:  *    particular capacity ΓÇö see `Role`. This is what lets one card carry
17:  *    several unrelated signals: Goblin Sharpshooter is Goblin kindred because
18:  *    of its creature *type*, and part of the creature-death cluster because of
19:  *    its *text*, and those two facts have nothing to do with each other.
20:  *
21:  * 2. TWO SIDES. Membership in a group is read off structured data wherever it
22:  *    exists (creature types, keywords, type line); qualifying as a *payoff*
23:  *    is read off rules text. A card's NAME is never evidence of anything ΓÇö
24:  *    see `stripSelfReferences` for why that mattered.
25:  *
26:  * 3. QUALIFIERS. A payoff can be restricted to a subtype, and then it only
27:  *    pays off cards of that subtype. Sliver Gravemother cares about Slivers
28:  *    in the graveyard, so it feeds "Reanimator (Sliver)" ΓÇö not generic
29:  *    Reanimator ΓÇö and every non-Sliver creature in your bin is worth nothing
30:  *    to it.
31:  *
32:  * Extending this: adding an archetype means adding one entry to `ARCHETYPES`
33:  * with per-role matchers. `Role`, `QualifierKind` and the catalog are all
34:  * meant to grow; nothing here is closed.
35:  */
36: import type { CardRow } from '../types';
37: 
38: /**
39:  * The capacity in which a card participates in an archetype.
40:  *
41:  * KNOWN LIMITATION ΓÇö this vocabulary is provisional and wants review. It
42:  * replaces an earlier "Outlet / Payoff" split that was reported as "not quite
43:  * right", and these five are an inference from worked examples rather than a
44:  * model anyone has signed off on. The specific problem with Outlet/Payoff was
45:  * that the two are almost never separable on a real card: Lathril's activated
46:  * ability *consumes* ten Elves and *rewards* you in the same breath, and
47:  * Viscera Seer is a sacrifice outlet whose whole point is the scry it gives
48:  * back. Splitting "consumes" from "rewards" lets one ability be both, which
49:  * Outlet/Payoff could not express.
50:  *
51:  * Cases known to still sit awkwardly:
52:  *  - Goblin Sharpshooter reads as `rewards` on creature-death here (it untaps
53:  *    when a creature dies), but it's often *described* as a sacrifice outlet,
54:  *    because with any outlet it becomes a machine gun. The card enables a
55:  *    loop it does not itself contain, and no role below captures "enables".
56:  *  - `is` on a vanilla creature is deliberately not wired into Aristocrats,
57:  *    even though a vanilla creature genuinely is sacrifice fodder ΓÇö counting
58:  *    it would make every creature deck read as Aristocrats.
59:  */
60: export type Role =
61:   /** The card *is* the resource: a Goblin, an Equipment, a land. Structured
62:    * data, never text. Passive ΓÇö see `ACTIVE_ROLES`. */
63:   | 'is'
64:   /** The card *makes* the resource: Goblin tokens, extra land drops, cards
65:    * into your own graveyard. */
66:   | 'produces'
67:   /** The card *needs* the resource, as a cost or a requirement: "Sacrifice a
68:    * creature:", "Tap ten untapped Elves:". */
69:   | 'consumes'
70:   /** The card *benefits* from the resource existing or the event happening:
71:    * Blood Artist, Craterhoof Behemoth, Teysa buffing your tokens. */
72:   | 'rewards'
73:   /** The card *doubles or repeats* the resource or event: Doubling Season,
74:    * Teysa making death triggers fire twice. A card that only amplifies needs
75:    * something else to amplify ΓÇö it generates no value alone. */
76:   | 'amplifies';
77: 
78: export const ROLES: Role[] = ['is', 'produces', 'consumes', 'rewards', 'amplifies'];
79: 
80: /**
81:  * Roles that mean the card actually engages with the plan, as opposed to
82:  * merely being a member of a group.
83:  *
84:  * This is the generalisation of the old "cares, not shares" kindred rule: a
85:  * commander needs at least one active role to be suggested for an archetype.
86:  * Silas Renn *is* a Human (`is`) and never mentions Humans, so he is not a
87:  * Human commander. Krenko *produces* Goblins and *rewards* having them, so he
88:  * is. The same test now covers keywords for free ΓÇö having Trample is `is`,
89:  * granting it to your team is `produces`.
90:  */
91: export const ACTIVE_ROLES: Role[] = ['produces', 'consumes', 'rewards', 'amplifies'];
92: 
93: export function hasActiveRole(roles: Role[]): boolean {
94:   return roles.some((r) => ACTIVE_ROLES.includes(r));
95: }
96: 
97: /** What a qualifier narrows a signal to. Open to growth ΓÇö card types and
98:  * permanent types are the obvious next two. */
99: export type QualifierKind = 'creatureType' | 'keyword';
100: 
101: /** One archetype a card participates in, with the capacities it does so in. */
102: export interface SignalMatch {
103:   archetype: string;
104:   label: string;
105:   description: string;
106:   weight: number;
107:   /** Present when the signal is restricted ΓÇö "Reanimator (Sliver)". */
108:   qualifier?: string;
109:   qualifierKind?: QualifierKind;
110:   roles: Role[];
111: }
112: 
113: /**
114:  * Identifies one archetype, including its qualifier where it has one.
115:  *
116:  * The minimal shape a `SignalMatch` satisfies structurally, so callers that
117:  * only want to *name* an archetype ΓÇö "fetch me everything tagged
118:  * kindred:Goblin" ΓÇö don't have to invent a whole match to do it.
119:  */
120: export interface SignalKey {
121:   archetype: string;
122:   qualifier?: string;
123: }
124: 
125: /** A signal's stable identity, so the same archetype at different qualifiers
126:  * counts as different signals. */
127: export function signalKey({ archetype, qualifier }: SignalKey): string {
128:   return qualifier ? `${archetype}:${qualifier}` : archetype;
129: }
130: 
131: /** One card that participates in a requested archetype, and how. */
132: export interface SignalCandidate {
133:   row: CardRow;
134:   roles: Role[];
135: }
136: 
137: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
138: // Card facts
139: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
140: 
141: /** Everything the matchers below are allowed to look at. */
142: export interface CardFacts {
143:   name: string;
144:   typeLine: string;
145:   /** Oracle text with the card's own name(s) removed. Match against this. */
146:   text: string;
147:   /** Oracle text as printed. Only for facts that need to see a self-reference,
148:    * like `sacrificesItself`. */
149:   rawText: string;
150:   creatureTypes: string[];
151:   keywords: string[];
152:   /** Creature types this card creates tokens of. "Create two 1/1 red Goblin
153:    * creature tokens" makes Krenko's Command a Goblin card despite a Sorcery
154:    * having no creature types of its own. */
155:   producedTokenTypes: string[];
156:   /** The card sacrifices *itself* ΓÇö a fetch land, a Blood Crypt-style cost.
157:    * Distinct from sacrificing an indefinite object, which is the Aristocrats
158:    * pattern. */
159:   sacrificesItself: boolean;
160:   isLand: boolean;
161:   isCreature: boolean;
162:   isEquipment: boolean;
163:   isAura: boolean;
164: }
165: 
166: /**
167:  * Removes the card's own name from its oracle text.
168:  *
169:  * A card's rules text refers to itself by name, so any check that regexes a
170:  * word against oracle text will match that word for free when it appears in
171:  * the name. Goblin Sharpshooter's abilities are "doesn't untap", "whenever a
172:  * creature dies, untap" and a ping ΓÇö it does not care about Goblins in the
173:  * slightest ΓÇö yet it matched Goblin kindred purely because "Goblin" is in its
174:  * name. Names are not abilities, so they are removed before anything reads
175:  * the text.
176:  *
177:  * Both the full name and the pre-comma short form go, since rules text uses
178:  * the short form ("Lathril" for "Lathril, Blade of the Elves").
179:  */
180: export function stripSelfReferences(text: string, ...names: (string | null)[]): string {
181:   let out = text;
182:   const forms = new Set<string>();
183:   for (const name of names) {
184:     if (!name) continue;
185:     forms.add(name);
186:     // "Lathril, Blade of the Elves" -> also strip "Lathril".
187:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
188:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
189:     if (short && short !== name) forms.add(short);
190:   }
191:   // Longest first, so the full name goes before its own short form.
192:   for (const form of [...forms].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
193:     out = out.split(form).join(' ');
194:   }
195:   return out;
196: }
197: 
198: function parseJsonArray(value: string | null): string[] {
199:   if (!value) return [];
200:   try {
201:     const parsed = JSON.parse(value);
202:     return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [];
203:   } catch {
204:     return [];
205:   }
206: }
207: 
208: /** Every word in a piece of text, lowercased. The unit of vocabulary
209:  * lookup ΓÇö see `candidateTypes` for why looking up beats searching. */
210: function wordsIn(text: string): string[] {
211:   return text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z][a-z'-]*/g) ?? [];
212: }
213: 
214: /**
215:  * Creature types of tokens this card creates.
216:  *
217:  * Read out of each "create ... token" clause, so a type mentioned elsewhere
218:  * in an unrelated sentence isn't credited as a token type.
219:  */
220: function findProducedTokenTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
221:   const found = new Set<string>();
222:   for (const clause of text.match(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi) ?? []) {
223:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
224:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
225:       if (type) found.add(type);
226:     }
227:   }
228:   return [...found];
229: }
230: 
231: /**
232:  * The creature types on a card, from its type line.
233:  *
234:  * Two filters, because either one alone lets junk through:
235:  *
236:  *   1. **Only Creature and Kindred cards have creature types** (CR 205.3m).
237:  *      Every other card type has its own subtype list. "Battle ΓÇö Control
238:  *      Point" made *Control* a creature type, so every card reading "creatures
239:  *      you control" was detected as caring about Control Kindred, and a real
240:  *      30-card list came back with a 14-card "Control Kindred" theme.
241:  *
242:  *   2. **The subtypes of a Creature card are still not all creature types.**
243:  *      They are mixed together and not positionally separable: "Artifact
244:  *      Creature ΓÇö Equipment Boar" and "Kindred Enchantment ΓÇö Lhurgoyf Aura"
245:  *      each carry one of each. That made Equipment, Aura, and Saga creature
246:  *      types, and produced a three-card "Aura Kindred" theme on a graveyard
247:  *      list.
248:  *
249:  * `knownTypes` is Scryfall's creature-type catalog, fetched alongside the bulk
250:  * data. Omitting it falls back to filter 1 only, which is what a database
251:  * seeded before the catalog existed gets ΓÇö narrower than nothing, and it
252:  * degrades rather than failing.
253:  */
254: export function parseCreatureTypes(typeLine: string, knownTypes?: Set<string>): string[] {
255:   const [typePart, subtypePart] = typeLine.split('ΓÇö');
256:   if (!subtypePart) return [];
257:   // typePart is always populated: .split() on any string returns at least
258:   // one element, which destructures into this position.
259:   // Word-boundary matched, and checked against the type part only: a Battle
260:   // whose subtype happened to read "Creature" would otherwise slip through.
261:   if (!/\b(Creature|Kindred|Tribal)\b/.test(typePart!)) return [];
262: 
263:   const words = subtypePart.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
264:   return knownTypes ? words.filter((word) => knownTypes.has(word)) : words;
265: }
266: 
267: /**
268:  * Lookup tables for the vocabulary signal detection recognises.
269:  *
270:  * Built once and reused across every card. The point is direction: with a
271:  * map, recognising a card's types costs one lookup per word it contains;
272:  * without one, it cost a regex per type in Magic. Across the card pool that
273:  * was the difference between ~8 seconds and ~82.
274:  */
275: export interface Vocabulary {
276:   /** Lowercased word, singular or plural, to its canonical creature type:
277:    * "elves" and "elf" both map to "Elf". */
278:   typeByWord: Map<string, string>;
279:   /** Lowercased single-word keyword to its canonical form. */
280:   keywordByWord: Map<string, string>;
281:   /** Keywords containing a space, which single-word lookup cannot find. */
282:   multiWordKeywords: string[];
283: }
284: 
285: export function buildVocabulary(creatureTypes: string[], keywords: string[]): Vocabulary {
286:   const typeByWord = new Map<string, string>();
287:   for (const type of creatureTypes) {
288:     typeByWord.set(type.toLowerCase(), type);
289:     typeByWord.set(pluralOfType(type).toLowerCase(), type);
290:   }
291: 
292:   const keywordByWord = new Map<string, string>();
293:   const multiWordKeywords: string[] = [];
294:   for (const keyword of keywords) {
295:     if (keyword.includes(' ')) multiWordKeywords.push(keyword);
296:     else keywordByWord.set(keyword.toLowerCase(), keyword);
297:   }
298: 
299:   return { typeByWord, keywordByWord, multiWordKeywords };
300: }
301: 
302: const wordPatternCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
303: 
304: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
305:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
306: }
307: 
308: /**
309:  * The English plural of a creature type, because cards refer to a type in the
310:  * aggregate ΓÇö "Elves you control", not "Elf you control". Only the irregular
311:  * endings Magic's type list actually contains are handled.
312:  */
313: export function pluralOfType(type: string): string {
314:   // Elf -> Elves, Dwarf -> Dwarves. Lathril says "ten untapped Elves you
315:   // control", so missing this drops one of the format's best-known kindred
316:   // commanders.
317:   if (/f$/i.test(type)) return type.replace(/f$/i, 'ves');
318:   // Sphinx -> Sphinxes, Fungus -> Funguses, Leech -> Leeches.
319:   if (/(s|x|z|ch|sh)$/i.test(type)) return `${type}es`;
320:   return `${type}s`;
321: }
322: 
323: const tokenDescriptorCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
324: 
325: /**
326:  * A token's printed type line inside a "create" clause ΓÇö "Goblin creature
327:  * tokens", "Elf Warrior creature tokens". One optional intervening word so a
328:  * token with two creature types still matches.
329:  */
330: function tokenDescriptorPattern(type: string): RegExp {
331:   let pattern = tokenDescriptorCache.get(type);
332:   if (!pattern) {
333:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(type)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(type))})`;
334:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${forms}(?:\\s+\\w+)?\\s+(?:creature\\s+)?tokens?\\b`, 'gi');
335:     tokenDescriptorCache.set(type, pattern);
336:   }
337:   // Shared cached regex with /g ΓÇö reset before each use.
338:   pattern.lastIndex = 0;
339:   return pattern;
340: }
341: 
342: /** Matches a word or its plural, on a word boundary. Cached: this runs against
343:  * every candidate in a pool of thousands. */
344: function wordPattern(word: string): RegExp {
345:   let pattern = wordPatternCache.get(word);
346:   if (!pattern) {
347:     pattern = new RegExp(
348:       `\\b(?:${escapeRegExp(word)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(word))})\\b`,
349:       'i',
350:     );
351:     wordPatternCache.set(word, pattern);
352:   }
353:   return pattern;
354: }
355: 
356: /**
357:  * Whether the card sacrifices *itself*, as opposed to an indefinite object.
358:  *
359:  * Two spellings, because Scryfall changed theirs. Older text named the card
360:  * ("Sacrifice Arid Mesa:"); current text says "Sacrifice this land:" /
361:  * "Sacrifice this creature:". Both are read off the RAW text ΓÇö the
362:  * name-stripped copy renders the first form as a bare "Sacrifice :".
363:  */
364: function detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText: string, name: string): boolean {
365:   if (/\bsacrifice this\b/i.test(rawText)) return true;
366:   // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
367:   const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
368:   if (!short) return false;
369:   return new RegExp(`sacrifice ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(rawText);
370: }
371: 
372: /**
373:  * Removes reminder text ΓÇö the parenthetical restatement of a keyword.
374:  *
375:  * Reminder text explains a keyword the card already has; it is never an
376:  * ability of its own. Leaving it in produced real false positives: Sliver
377:  * Gravemother's Encore reminder text ends "They gain haste", which read as
378:  * the card *granting* haste to your team, i.e. an active Haste payoff.
379:  */
380: function stripReminderText(text: string): string {
381:   return text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ');
382: }
383: 
384: export function buildCardFacts(row: CardRow, vocab: Vocabulary): CardFacts {
385:   const rawText = row.oracle_text ?? '';
386:   const text = stripReminderText(stripSelfReferences(rawText, row.name, row.back_name ?? null));
387:   const typeLine = row.type_line ?? '';
388:   return {
389:     name: row.name,
390:     typeLine,
391:     text,
392:     rawText,
393:     creatureTypes: parseJsonArray(row.creature_types),
394:     keywords: parseJsonArray(row.keywords),
395:     producedTokenTypes: findProducedTokenTypes(text, vocab),
396:     sacrificesItself: detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText, row.name),
397:     isLand: /\bLand\b/.test(typeLine),
398:     isCreature: /\bCreature\b/.test(typeLine),
399:     isEquipment: /\bEquipment\b/.test(typeLine),
400:     isAura: /\bAura\b/.test(typeLine),
401:   };
402: }
403: 
404: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
405: // The archetype catalog
406: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
407: 
408: type Matcher = RegExp | ((f: CardFacts) => boolean);
409: 
410: export interface ArchetypeDef {
411:   key: string;
412:   label: string;
413:   description: string;
414:   weight: number;
415:   /** Per-role matchers. A card matching any matcher for a role gains it. */
416:   roles: Partial<Record<Role, Matcher[]>>;
417:   /**
418:    * When set, a match may be narrowed to a creature type the card's text
419:    * restricts it to ΓÇö the Sliver Gravemother case. A qualified signal only
420:    * counts supporters of that type, and separately implies kindred for it.
421:    */
422:   qualifiable?: QualifierKind;
423: }
424: 
425: function matches(matcher: Matcher, facts: CardFacts): boolean {
426:   return typeof matcher === 'function' ? matcher(facts) : matcher.test(facts.text);
427: }
428: 
429: /**
430:  * Archetypes keyed by their real names, because that's what a player would
431:  * call them. Kindred and keyword-care are generated per qualifier rather than

433:  *
434:  * Weights are a first pass and want tuning against real lists; they were set

436:  */
437: export const ARCHETYPES: ArchetypeDef[] = [

453:       rewards: [/(?:whenever|if)[^.;]*\b(?:dies|dying)\b/i],
454:       produces: [/create[^.;]*\bcreature token/i],

459:     key: 'goWide',

472:         /creature tokens you control (?:get|gain|have)/i,

514:       'Treating lands as a resource to be played, sacrificed, and recurred ΓÇö extra land drops, landfall ' +

632: /** Splits text into clauses, so a qualifier is only picked up from the same
633:  * sentence as the payoff it restricts. */
634: function clauses(text: string): string[] {
635:   return text.split(/[.;\n]/).filter((c) => c.trim().length > 0);
636: }
637: 
638: /**
639:  * The creature type a qualifiable archetype's payoff is restricted to, if any.
640:  *
641:  * Only a type mentioned in the same clause as the payoff counts ΓÇö a commander
642:  * that reanimates anything and separately happens to mention Goblins is not a
643:  * Goblin-restricted reanimator.
644:  */
645: function findQualifier(facts: CardFacts, def: ArchetypeDef, vocab: Vocabulary): string | undefined {
646:   const payoffMatchers = [...(def.roles.rewards ?? []), ...(def.roles.consumes ?? [])];
647:   for (const clause of clauses(facts.text)) {
648:     const hit = payoffMatchers.some((m) => (typeof m === 'function' ? false : m.test(clause)));
649:     if (!hit) continue;
650:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
651:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
652:       if (type) return type;
653:     }
654:   }
655:   return undefined;
656: }
657: 
658: function rolesFor(def: ArchetypeDef, facts: CardFacts): Role[] {
659:   const found: Role[] = [];
660:   for (const role of ROLES) {
661:     const matchers = def.roles[role];
662:     if (matchers?.some((m) => matches(m, facts))) found.push(role);
663:   }
664:   return found;
665: }
666: 
667: /**
668:  * The creature types a card could possibly relate to.
669:  *
670:  * Derived from the card outward rather than by testing every type in the
671:  * game against it. That is not just an optimisation: looping the full
672:  * vocabulary meant 647 types x 884 keywords of regex per card, which took
673:  * 82 seconds across the card pool and made precomputing signals impractical.
674:  * Scanning the card's own words and intersecting with the known-type set is
675:  * proportional to the card, not to Magic's type list.
676:  */
677: function candidateTypes(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
678:   const found = new Set<string>();
679:   // Structured, and free.
680:   for (const type of facts.creatureTypes) found.add(type);
681:   for (const type of facts.producedTokenTypes) found.add(type);
682:   // Textual: every word the card uses, looked up rather than searched for.
683:   for (const word of wordsIn(facts.text)) {
684:     const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
685:     if (type) found.add(type);
686:   }
687:   return [...found];
688: }

690: /** Kindred, one signal per creature type. Membership is structural (the card's
691:  * own type, or a token type it makes); caring about the type is textual. */
692: function detectKindred(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): SignalMatch[] {
693:   const out: SignalMatch[] = [];
694:   for (const type of candidateTypes(facts, vocab)) {
695:     const roles: Role[] = [];
696:     // Structured data only ΓÇö never the name. Goblin Sharpshooter is a Goblin
697:     // because its type line says so.
698:     if (facts.creatureTypes.includes(type)) roles.push('is');
699:     // "Create two 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens" makes Krenko's Command a
700:     // Goblin card even though a Sorcery has no creature type.
701:     if (facts.producedTokenTypes.includes(type)) roles.push('produces');
702: 
703:     // Naming the token's type is not caring about the type ΓÇö "create two 1/1
704:     // red Goblin creature tokens" already counted as `produces` above, and
705:     // must not also read as a payoff. Krenko's Command says "Goblin" exactly
706:     // once, in the token's name, and is a producer only; Krenko, Mob Boss
707:     // says it twice ΓÇö once naming the token, once counting "the number of
708:     // Goblins you control" ΓÇö and that second mention is the payoff.
709:     const caringText = facts.text.replace(tokenDescriptorPattern(type), ' ');
710: 
711:     for (const clause of clauses(caringText)) {
712:       if (!wordPattern(type).test(clause)) continue;
713:       const consumesType = /\bsacrifice\b|\btap\b|\bdiscard\b|\bexile\b/i.test(clause);
714:       if (consumesType) {
715:         roles.push('consumes');
716:         // An activated ability is "cost: effect", so a clause that spends the
717:         // type also hands something back. Lathril's "Tap ten untapped Elves
718:         // you control: Each opponent loses 10 life" consumes Elves *and*
719:         // rewards you for having had them.
720:         if (clause.includes(':')) roles.push('rewards');
721:       }
722:       if (
723:         /\bget\b|\bgains?\b|\bhas\b|\bhave\b|whenever|for each|number of|search|\blose\b|\bloses\b/i.test(
724:           clause,
725:         )
726:       ) {
727:         roles.push('rewards');
728:       }
729:       // Mentioned outside a token's name, in a way none of the above caught ΓÇö
730:       // still active interest in the type, which is what separates Krenko
731:       // from Silas Renn.
732:       if (!consumesType && !roles.includes('rewards')) roles.push('rewards');
733:     }

735:     if (roles.length === 0) continue;

737:       archetype: 'kindred',
738:       label: `${type} Kindred`,
739:       description: `${pluralOfType(type)}, and cards that care about having them.`,
740:       weight: 15,
741:       qualifier: type,
742:       qualifierKind: 'creatureType',
743:       roles: [...new Set(roles)],
744:     });
745:   }
746:   return out;

749: /**
750:  * Keyword care, one signal per keyword.
751:  *
752:  * A keyword on its own is not a synergy ΓÇö Trample is a good thing to have,
753:  * not a deck. What matters is a commander that *cares* about the keyword
754:  * (grants it, or triggers off it), which is the same active-role test kindred
755:  * uses. Having the keyword is `is` and never qualifies a commander on its own.
756:  */
757: function detectKeywordCare(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): SignalMatch[] {
758:   const out: SignalMatch[] = [];
759:   for (const keyword of candidateKeywords(facts, vocab)) {
760:     if (EXCLUDED_KEYWORDS.has(keyword.toLowerCase())) continue;
761:     const roles: Role[] = [];
762:     if (facts.keywords.includes(keyword)) roles.push('is');
763:     const pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${escapeRegExp(keyword)}\\b`, 'i');
764:     for (const clause of clauses(facts.text)) {
765:       if (!pattern.test(clause)) continue;

767:       // others, which is the Craterhoof shape.
768:       if (/\b(?:gains?|have|has|gets?)\b/i.test(clause)) roles.push('produces');
769:       if (/whenever|for each|number of/i.test(clause)) roles.push('rewards');
770:     }
771:     if (roles.length === 0) continue;
772:     out.push({
773:       archetype: 'keywordCare',
774:       label: keyword,
775:       description: `Cards with ${keyword}, where the commander actually cares about it.`,
776:       weight: 8,
777:       qualifier: keyword,
778:       qualifierKind: 'keyword',
779:       roles: [...new Set(roles)],
780:     });
781:   }
782:   return out;
783: }
784: 
785: /**
786:  * Keywords that are structural rather than thematic.
787:  *
788:  * The Partner family says who can be your commander, not what your deck
789:  * wants to do. Surfacing "Partner" as a shared keyword would be a confusing
790:  * echo of the dedicated partner/background handling rather than a second,
791:  * unrelated signal.
792:  */
793: const EXCLUDED_KEYWORDS = new Set([
794:   'partner',
795:   'partner with',
796:   'friends forever',
797:   'choose a background',
798:   "doctor's companion",
799: ]);
800: 
801: /** The keywords a card could possibly relate to. Same inversion as
802:  * `candidateTypes` ΓÇö look up the card's own words instead of testing all 884
803:  * keywords against it. Multi-word keywords ("first strike") can't be found by
804:  * single-word lookup, so those few are still tested directly. */
805: function candidateKeywords(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
806:   const found = new Set<string>();
807:   for (const keyword of facts.keywords) found.add(keyword);
808:   for (const word of wordsIn(facts.text)) {
809:     const keyword = vocab.keywordByWord.get(word);
810:     if (keyword) found.add(keyword);
811:   }
812:   const lowerText = facts.text.toLowerCase();
813:   for (const keyword of vocab.multiWordKeywords) {
814:     if (lowerText.includes(keyword.toLowerCase())) found.add(keyword);
815:   }
816:   return [...found];
817: }
818: 
819: /** Every archetype this card participates in, and how. */
820: export function detectSignals(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): SignalMatch[] {
821:   const out: SignalMatch[] = [];
822: 
823:   for (const def of ARCHETYPES) {
824:     const roles = rolesFor(def, facts);
825:     if (roles.length === 0) continue;
826:     const qualifier = def.qualifiable ? findQualifier(facts, def, vocab) : undefined;
827:     out.push({
828:       archetype: def.key,
829:       label: qualifier ? `${def.label} (${qualifier})` : def.label,
830:       description: def.description,
831:       weight: def.weight,
832:       qualifier,
833:       qualifierKind: qualifier ? def.qualifiable : undefined,
834:       roles,
835:     });
836:   }
837: 
838:   out.push(...detectKindred(facts, vocab));
839:   out.push(...detectKeywordCare(facts, vocab));
840:   return out;
841: }

843: /**
844:  * Whether a card in the list can support a signal the commander showed.
845:  *
846:  * Unqualified signals accept any card that participates in the archetype at
847:  * all. A *qualified* signal additionally requires the supporter to be of that
848:  * subtype ΓÇö this is the Sliver Gravemother rule, and it is the whole reason
849:  * qualifiers exist.
850:  */
851: export function supports(signal: SignalMatch, supporter: SignalMatch[], facts: CardFacts): boolean {
852:   const sameArchetype = supporter.filter((s) => s.archetype === signal.archetype);
853:   if (sameArchetype.length === 0) return false;
854:   if (!signal.qualifier) return true;
855: 
856:   if (signal.qualifierKind === 'creatureType') {
857:     return (
858:       facts.creatureTypes.includes(signal.qualifier) ||
859:       facts.producedTokenTypes.includes(signal.qualifier)
860:     );
861:   }
862:   if (signal.qualifierKind === 'keyword') {
863:     return facts.keywords.includes(signal.qualifier);
864:   }
865:   return sameArchetype.some((s) => s.qualifier === signal.qualifier);

869:  * Presentation details for a signal read back out of storage.

871:  * The `card_signals` table records what a card *is* ΓÇö archetype, qualifier,
872:  * roles ΓÇö and deliberately not how to label it. Labels and weights are
873:  * presentation, and storing them would mean a reworded description needed a
874:  * full re-import to take effect. This rebuilds them from the catalog instead.
875:  */
876: export function archetypeDisplay(
877:   archetype: string,
878:   qualifier: string | null,

881:     return {
882:       label: `${qualifier} Kindred`,
883:       description: `${pluralOfType(qualifier)}, and cards that care about having them.`,
884:       weight: 15,

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions ΓÇö
including Partner/Background pairs ΓÇö with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time ΓÇö the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first ΓÇö it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score ΓÇö see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander ΓÇö see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card

/**
 * The signal model: what a card contributes to a deck's plan, and in what
 * capacity.
 *
 * This replaces the old flat "theme" model, in which a signal was a single
 * regex applied identically to your card and to the candidate commander, and
 * two cards "synergised" when the same words appeared in both. That measured
 * lexical co-occurrence rather than synergy: "Sacrifice a creature" and
 * "Sacrifice Arid Mesa" are the same word and completely different mechanics,
 * and a commander that pays off a plan (Craterhoof Behemoth pumping your
 * board) usually shares no vocabulary at all with the cards that set it up.
 *
 * Three ideas do the work here.
 *
 * 1. ROLES. A card doesn't just "have" a theme, it participates in one in a
 *    particular capacity ΓÇö see `Role`. This is what lets one card carry
 *    several unrelated signals: Goblin Sharpshooter is Goblin kindred because
 *    of its creature *type*, and part of the creature-death cluster because of
 *    its *text*, and those two facts have nothing to do with each other.
 *

57: /** Detect against a vocabulary containing these creature types / keywords. */
58: function signalsFor(
59:   row: CardRow,
60:   creatureTypes: string[] = [],
61:   keywords: string[] = [],
62: ): SignalMatch[] {
63:   const vocab = buildVocabulary(creatureTypes, keywords);
64:   return detectSignals(buildCardFacts(row, vocab), vocab);

67: function find(
68:   signals: SignalMatch[],
69:   archetype: string,
70:   qualifier?: string,

72:   return signals.find((s) => s.archetype === archetype && s.qualifier === qualifier);
73: }

75: function rolesOf(signals: SignalMatch[], archetype: string, qualifier?: string): Role[] {
76:   return (find(signals, archetype, qualifier)?.roles ?? []).slice().sort();
77: }

part.text:
## Objective
Fix the `parseCreatureTypes` function in `signals.ts` so multi-word creature types (like "Time Lord") present in `knownTypes` are recognized and kept as single strings, while single-word types still work correctly, and partial multi-word matches (e.g., "Time" alone when only "Time Lord" is known) are not kept.

## Important Details
- The bug is in `apps/commander-recommender/server/src/services/signals.ts` line 263: `words.filter((word) => knownTypes.has(word))` splits on whitespace and checks each word individually, so "Time Lord" becomes `['Time', 'Lord']` and can never match the known type "Time Lord".
- Test requirements: 
  1. Multi-word type present in knownTypes should be recognized and kept as one string
  2. Ordinary single-word type should work exactly as before  
  3. A word that is the first word of a multi-word type but not followed by the rest should NOT be kept on its own (e.g., "Time Wizard" where only "Time Lord" is known ΓåÆ neither "Time" nor the pair should be kept)
- Also in `partners.ts`, Doctor's companion uses exact set equality against `{'Time Lord', 'Doctor'}`, creating an inconsistency that the fix should address.
- The Scryfall creature-types.json catalog does contain multi-word entries like "Time Lord".

## Work State

### Completed
- (none)

### Active
- Current `parseCreatureTypes` (line 254-265 in signals.ts) splits subtypePart on whitespace: `subtypePart.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)`, then filters each word individually against `knownTypes`

### Blocked  
- Need to determine the correct algorithm: should check for exact multi-word matches first, then fall back to single-word matching, ensuring that a word only kept if it's independently in knownTypes OR it's the start of a recognized multi-word sequence

## Next Move
1. **Immediate**: Modify `parseCreatureTypes` in `signals.ts` to handle multi-word types: first attempt to match consecutive word sequences against `knownTypes` (longest match first), then fall back to individual word matching. This ensures "Time Lord" is kept as one entry, single words like "Goblin" still work, and "Time" alone isn't kept when only "Time Lord" is known.
2. **Add/update tests** in `signals.test.ts` exercising the three cases (multi-word recognition, single-word unchanged, partial multi-word NOT kept).
3. **Run** `npm test` for the signals package to verify all tests pass.

## Relevant Files
- `M:\Projects\dev-docs\tests\.worktrees\kane-02-multiword-creature-type\apps\commander-recommender\server\src\services\signals.ts` ΓÇö contains `parseCreatureTypes` at line 254; modify the word-splitting and filtering logic
- `M:\Projects\dev-docs\tests\.worktrees\kane-02-multiword-creature-type\apps\commander-recommender\server\src\services\signals.test.ts` ΓÇö add/ update tests for the three cases
- `M:\Projects\dev-docs\tests\.worktrees\kane-02-multiword-creature-type\apps\commander-recommender\server\data\creature-types.json` ΓÇö Scryfall catalog with multi-word entries like "Time Lord"
- `M:\Projects\dev-docs\tests\.worktrees\kane-02-multiword-creature-type\apps\commander-recommender\server\src\services\partners.ts` ΓÇö Doctor's companion check that uses exact `{'Time Lord', 'Doctor'}` set equality
Continue if you have next steps, or stop and ask for clarification if you are unsure how to proceed.

<content>
1: /**
2:  * The signal model: what a card contributes to a deck's plan, and in what
3:  * capacity.
4:  *
5:  * This replaces the old flat "theme" model, in which a signal was a single
6:  * regex applied identically to your card and to the candidate commander, and
7:  * two cards "synergised" when the same words appeared in both. That measured
8:  * lexical co-occurrence rather than synergy: "Sacrifice a creature" and
9:  * "Sacrifice Arid Mesa" are the same word and completely different mechanics,
10:  * and a commander that pays off a plan (Craterhoof Behemoth pumping your
11:  * board) usually shares no vocabulary at all with the cards that set it up.
12:  *
13:  * Three ideas do the work here.
14:  *
15:  * 1. ROLES. A card doesn't just "have" a theme, it participates in one in a
16:  *    particular capacity ΓÇö see `Role`. This is what lets one card carry
17:  *    several unrelated signals: Goblin Sharpshooter is Goblin kindred because
18:  *    of its creature *type*, and part of the creature-death cluster because of
19:  *    its *text*, and those two facts have nothing to do with each other.
20:  *
21:  * 2. TWO SIDES. Membership in a group is read off structured data wherever it
22:  *    exists (creature types, keywords, type line); qualifying as a *payoff*
23:  *    is read off rules text. A card's NAME is never evidence of anything ΓÇö
24:  *    see `stripSelfReferences` for why that mattered.
25:  *
26:  * 3. QUALIFIERS. A payoff can be restricted to a subtype, and then it only
27:  *    pays off cards of that subtype. Sliver Gravemother cares about Slivers
28:  *    in the graveyard, so it feeds "Reanimator (Sliver)" ΓÇö not generic
29:  *    Reanimator ΓÇö and every non-Sliver creature in your bin is worth nothing
30:  *    to it.
31:  *
32:  * Extending this: adding an archetype means adding one entry to `ARCHETYPES`
33:  * with per-role matchers. `Role`, `QualifierKind` and the catalog are all
34:  * meant to grow; nothing here is closed.
35:  */
36: import type { CardRow } from '../types';
37: 
38: /**
39:  * The capacity in which a card participates in an archetype.
40:  *
41:  * KNOWN LIMITATION ΓÇö this vocabulary is provisional and wants review. It
42:  * replaces an earlier "Outlet / Payoff" split that was reported as "not quite
43:  * right", and these five are an inference from worked examples rather than a
44:  * model anyone has signed off on. The specific problem with Outlet/Payoff was
45:  * that the two are almost never separable on a real card: Lathril's activated
46:  * ability *consumes* ten Elves and *rewards* you in the same breath, and
47:  * Viscera Seer is a sacrifice outlet whose whole point is the scry it gives
48:  * back. Splitting "consumes" from "rewards" lets one ability be both, which
49:  * Outlet/Payoff could not express.
50:  *
51:  * Cases known to still sit awkwardly:
52:  *  - Goblin Sharpshooter reads as `rewards` on creature-death here (it untaps
53:  *    when a creature dies), but it's often *described* as a sacrifice outlet,
54:  *    because with any outlet it becomes a machine gun. The card enables a
55:  *    loop it does not itself contain, and no role below captures "enables".
56:  *  - `is` on a vanilla creature is deliberately not wired into Aristocrats,
57:  *    even though a vanilla creature genuinely is sacrifice fodder ΓÇö counting
58:  *    it would make every creature deck read as Aristocrats.
59:  */
60: export type Role =
61:   /** The card *is* the resource: a Goblin, an Equipment, a land. Structured
62:    * data, never text. Passive ΓÇö see `ACTIVE_ROLES`. */
63:   | 'is'
64:   /** The card *makes* the resource: Goblin tokens, extra land drops, cards
65:    * into your own graveyard. */
66:   | 'produces'
67:   /** The card *needs* the resource, as a cost or a requirement: "Sacrifice a
68:    * creature:", "Tap ten untapped Elves:". */
69:   | 'consumes'
70:   /** The card *benefits* from the resource existing or the event happening:
71:    * Blood Artist, Craterhoof Behemoth, Teysa buffing your tokens. */
72:   | 'rewards'
73:   /** The card *doubles or repeats* the resource or event: Doubling Season,
74:    * Teysa making death triggers fire twice. A card that only amplifies needs
75:    * something else to amplify ΓÇö it generates no value alone. */
76:   | 'amplifies';
77: 
78: export const ROLES: Role[] = ['is', 'produces', 'consumes', 'rewards', 'amplifies'];
79: 
80: /**
81:  * Roles that mean the card actually engages with the plan, as opposed to
82:  * merely being a member of a group.
83:  *
84:  * This is the generalisation of the old "cares, not shares" kindred rule: a
85:  * commander needs at least one active role to be suggested for an archetype.
86:  * Silas Renn *is* a Human (`is`) and never mentions Humans, so he is not a
87:  * Human commander. Krenko *produces* Goblins and *rewards* having them, so he
88:  * is. The same test now covers keywords for free ΓÇö having Trample is `is`,
89:  * granting it to your team is `produces`.
90:  */
91: export const ACTIVE_ROLES: Role[] = ['produces', 'consumes', 'rewards', 'amplifies'];
92: 
93: export function hasActiveRole(roles: Role[]): boolean {
94:   return roles.some((r) => ACTIVE_ROLES.includes(r));
95: }
96: 
97: /** What a qualifier narrows a signal to. Open to growth ΓÇö card types and
98:  * permanent types are the obvious next two. */
99: export type QualifierKind = 'creatureType' | 'keyword';
100: 
101: /** One archetype a card participates in, with the capacities it does so in. */
102: export interface SignalMatch {
103:   archetype: string;
104:   label: string;
105:   description: string;
106:   weight: number;
107:   /** Present when the signal is restricted ΓÇö "Reanimator (Sliver)". */
108:   qualifier?: string;
109:   qualifierKind?: QualifierKind;
110:   roles: Role[];
111: }
112: 
113: /**
114:  * Identifies one archetype, including its qualifier where it has one.
115:  *
116:  * The minimal shape a `SignalMatch` satisfies structurally, so callers that
117:  * only want to *name* an archetype ΓÇö "fetch me everything tagged
118:  * kindred:Goblin" ΓÇö don't have to invent a whole match to do it.
119:  */
120: export interface SignalKey {
121:   archetype: string;
122:   qualifier?: string;
123: }
124: 
125: /** A signal's stable identity, so the same archetype at different qualifiers
126:  * counts as different signals. */
127: export function signalKey({ archetype, qualifier }: SignalKey): string {
128:   return qualifier ? `${archetype}:${qualifier}` : archetype;
129: }
130: 
131: /** One card that participates in a requested archetype, and how. */
132: export interface SignalCandidate {
133:   row: CardRow;
134:   roles: Role[];
135: }
136: 
137: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
138: // Card facts
139: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
140: 
141: /** Everything the matchers below are allowed to look at. */
142: export interface CardFacts {
143:   name: string;
144:   typeLine: string;
145:   /** Oracle text with the card's own name(s) removed. Match against this. */
146:   text: string;
147:   /** Oracle text as printed. Only for facts that need to see a self-reference,
148:    * like `sacrificesItself`. */
149:   rawText: string;
150:   creatureTypes: string[];
151:   keywords: string[];
152:   /** Creature types this card creates tokens of. "Create two 1/1 red Goblin
153:    * creature tokens" makes Krenko's Command a Goblin card despite a Sorcery
154:    * having no creature types of its own. */
155:   producedTokenTypes: string[];
156:   /** The card sacrifices *itself* ΓÇö a fetch land, a Blood Crypt-style cost.
157:    * Distinct from sacrificing an indefinite object, which is the Aristocrats
158:    * pattern. */
159:   sacrificesItself: boolean;
160:   isLand: boolean;
161:   isCreature: boolean;
162:   isEquipment: boolean;
163:   isAura: boolean;
164: }
165: 
166: /**
167:  * Removes the card's own name from its oracle text.
168:  *
169:  * A card's rules text refers to itself by name, so any check that regexes a
170:  * word against oracle text will match that word for free when it appears in
171:  * the name. Goblin Sharpshooter's abilities are "doesn't untap", "whenever a
172:  * creature dies, untap" and a ping ΓÇö it does not care about Goblins in the
173:  * slightest ΓÇö yet it matched Goblin kindred purely because "Goblin" is in its
174:  * name. Names are not abilities, so they are removed before anything reads
175:  * the text.
176:  *
177:  * Both the full name and the pre-comma short form go, since rules text uses
178:  * the short form ("Lathril" for "Lathril, Blade of the Elves").
179:  */
180: export function stripSelfReferences(text: string, ...names: (string | null)[]): string {
181:   let out = text;
182:   const forms = new Set<string>();
183:   for (const name of names) {
184:     if (!name) continue;
185:     forms.add(name);
186:     // "Lathril, Blade of the Elves" -> also strip "Lathril".
187:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
188:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
189:     if (short && short !== name) forms.add(short);
190:   }
191:   // Longest first, so the full name goes before its own short form.
192:   for (const form of [...forms].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
193:     out = out.split(form).join(' ');
194:   }
195:   return out;
196: }
197: 
198: function parseJsonArray(value: string | null): string[] {
199:   if (!value) return [];
200:   try {
201:     const parsed = JSON.parse(value);
202:     return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [];
203:   } catch {
204:     return [];
205:   }
206: }
207: 
208: /** Every word in a piece of text, lowercased. The unit of vocabulary
209:  * lookup ΓÇö see `candidateTypes` for why looking up beats searching. */
210: function wordsIn(text: string): string[] {
211:   return text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z][a-z'-]*/g) ?? [];
212: }
213: 
214: /**
215:  * Creature types of tokens this card creates.
216:  *
217:  * Read out of each "create ... token" clause, so a type mentioned elsewhere
218:  * in an unrelated sentence isn't credited as a token type.
219:  */
220: function findProducedTokenTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
221:   const found = new Set<string>();
222:   for (const clause of text.match(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi) ?? []) {
223:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
224:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
225:       if (type) found.add(type);
226:     }
227:   }
228:   return [...found];
229: }
230: 
231: /**
232:  * The creature types on a card, from its type line.
233:  *
234:  * Two filters, because either one alone lets junk through:
235:  *
236:  *   1. **Only Creature and Kindred cards have creature types** (CR 205.3m).
237:  *      Every other card type has its own subtype list. "Battle ΓÇö Control
238:  *      Point" made *Control* a creature type, so every card reading "creatures
239:  *      you control" was detected as caring about Control Kindred, and a real
240:  *      30-card list came back with a 14-card "Control Kindred" theme.
241:  *
242:  *   2. **The subtypes of a Creature card are still not all creature types.**
243:  *      They are mixed together and not positionally separable: "Artifact
244:  *      Creature ΓÇö Equipment Boar" and "Kindred Enchantment ΓÇö Lhurgoyf Aura"
245:  *      each carry one of each. That made Equipment, Aura, and Saga creature
246:  *      types, and produced a three-card "Aura Kindred" theme on a graveyard
247:  *      list.
248:  *
249:  * `knownTypes` is Scryfall's creature-type catalog, fetched alongside the bulk
250:  * data. Omitting it falls back to filter 1 only, which is what a database
251:  * seeded before the catalog existed gets ΓÇö narrower than nothing, and it
252:  * degrades rather than failing.
253:  */
254: export function parseCreatureTypes(typeLine: string, knownTypes?: Set<string>): string[] {
255:   const [typePart, subtypePart] = typeLine.split('ΓÇö');
256:   if (!subtypePart) return [];
257:   // typePart is always populated: .split() on any string returns at least
258:   // one element, which destructures into this position.
259:   // Word-boundary matched, and checked against the type part only: a Battle
260:   // whose subtype happened to read "Creature" would otherwise slip through.
261:   if (!/\b(Creature|Kindred|Tribal)\b/.test(typePart!)) return [];
262: 
263:   const words = subtypePart.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
264:   return knownTypes ? words.filter((word) => knownTypes.has(word)) : words;
265: }
266: 
267: /**
268:  * Lookup tables for the vocabulary signal detection recognises.
269:  *
270:  * Built once and reused across every card. The point is direction: with a
271:  * map, recognising a card's types costs one lookup per word it contains;
272:  * without one, it cost a regex per type in Magic. Across the card pool that
273:  * was the difference between ~8 seconds and ~82.
274:  */
275: export interface Vocabulary {
276:   /** Lowercased word, singular or plural, to its canonical creature type:
277:    * "elves" and "elf" both map to "Elf". */
278:   typeByWord: Map<string, string>;
279:   /** Lowercased single-word keyword to its canonical form. */
280:   keywordByWord: Map<string, string>;
281:   /** Keywords containing a space, which single-word lookup cannot find. */
282:   multiWordKeywords: string[];
283: }
284: 
285: export function buildVocabulary(creatureTypes: string[], keywords: string[]): Vocabulary {
286:   const typeByWord = new Map<string, string>();
287:   for (const type of creatureTypes) {
288:     typeByWord.set(type.toLowerCase(), type);
289:     typeByWord.set(pluralOfType(type).toLowerCase(), type);
290:   }
291: 
292:   const keywordByWord = new Map<string, string>();
293:   const multiWordKeywords: string[] = [];
294:   for (const keyword of keywords) {
295:     if (keyword.includes(' ')) multiWordKeywords.push(keyword);
296:     else keywordByWord.set(keyword.toLowerCase(), keyword);
297:   }
298: 
299:   return { typeByWord, keywordByWord, multiWordKeywords };
300: }
301: 
302: const wordPatternCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
303: 
304: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
305:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
306: }
307: 
308: /**
309:  * The English plural of a creature type, because cards refer to a type in the
310:  * aggregate ΓÇö "Elves you control", not "Elf you control". Only the irregular
311:  * endings Magic's type list actually contains are handled.
312:  */
313: export function pluralOfType(type: string): string {
314:   // Elf -> Elves, Dwarf -> Dwarves. Lathril says "ten untapped Elves you
315:   // control", so missing this drops one of the format's best-known kindred
316:   // commanders.
317:   if (/f$/i.test(type)) return type.replace(/f$/i, 'ves');
318:   // Sphinx -> Sphinxes, Fungus -> Funguses, Leech -> Leeches.
319:   if (/(s|x|z|ch|sh)$/i.test(type)) return `${type}es`;
320:   return `${type}s`;
321: }
322: 
323: const tokenDescriptorCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
324: 
325: /**
326:  * A token's printed type line inside a "create" clause ΓÇö "Goblin creature
327:  * tokens", "Elf Warrior creature tokens". One optional intervening word so a
328:  * token with two creature types still matches.
329:  */
330: function tokenDescriptorPattern(type: string): RegExp {
331:   let pattern = tokenDescriptorCache.get(type);
332:   if (!pattern) {
333:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(type)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(type))})`;
334:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${forms}(?:\\s+\\w+)?\\s+(?:creature\\s+)?tokens?\\b`, 'gi');
335:     tokenDescriptorCache.set(type, pattern);
336:   }
337:   // Shared cached regex with /g ΓÇö reset before each use.
338:   pattern.lastIndex = 0;
339:   return pattern;
340: }
341: 
342: /** Matches a word or its plural, on a word boundary. Cached: this runs against
343:  * every candidate in a pool of thousands. */
344: function wordPattern(word: string): RegExp {
345:   let pattern = wordPatternCache.get(word);
346:   if (!pattern) {
347:     pattern = new RegExp(
348:       `\\b(?:${escapeRegExp(word)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(word))})\\b`,
349:       'i',
350:     );
351:     wordPatternCache.set(word, pattern);
352:   }
353:   return pattern;
354: }
355: 
356: /**
357:  * Whether the card sacrifices *itself*, as opposed to an indefinite object.
358:  *
359:  * Two spellings, because Scryfall changed theirs. Older text named the card
360:  * ("Sacrifice Arid Mesa:"); current text says "Sacrifice this land:" /
361:  * "Sacrifice this creature:". Both are read off the RAW text ΓÇö the
362:  * name-stripped copy renders the first form as a bare "Sacrifice :".
363:  */
364: function detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText: string, name: string): boolean {
365:   if (/\bsacrifice this\b/i.test(rawText)) return true;
366:   // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
367:   const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
368:   if (!short) return false;
369:   return new RegExp(`sacrifice ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(rawText);
370: }
371: 
372: /**
373:  * Removes reminder text ΓÇö the parenthetical restatement of a keyword.
374:  *
375:  * Reminder text explains a keyword the card already has; it is never an
376:  * ability of its own. Leaving it in produced real false positives: Sliver
377:  * Gravemother's Encore reminder text ends "They gain haste", which read as
378:  * the card *granting* haste to your team, i.e. an active Haste payoff.
379:  */
380: function stripReminderText(text: string): string {
381:   return text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ');
382: }
383: 
384: export function buildCardFacts(row: CardRow, vocab: Vocabulary): CardFacts {
385:   const rawText = row.oracle_text ?? '';
386:   const text = stripReminderText(stripSelfReferences(rawText, row.name, row.back_name ?? null));
387:   const typeLine = row.type_line ?? '';
388:   return {
389:     name: row.name,
390:     typeLine,
391:     text,
392:     rawText,
393:     creatureTypes: parseJsonArray(row.creature_types),
394:     keywords: parseJsonArray(row.keywords),
395:     producedTokenTypes: findProducedTokenTypes(text, vocab),
396:     sacrificesItself: detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText, row.name),
397:     isLand: /\bLand\b/.test(typeLine),
398:     isCreature: /\bCreature\b/.test(typeLine),
399:     isEquipment: /\bEquipment\b/.test(typeLine),
400:     isAura: /\bAura\b/.test(typeLine),
401:   };
402: }

408: type Matcher = RegExp | ((f: CardFacts) => boolean);

410: export interface ArchetypeDef {
411:   key: string;
412:   label: string;
413:   description: string;
414:   weight: number;
415:   /** Per-role matchers. A card matching any matcher for a role gains it. */

419:    * restricts it to ΓÇö the Sliver Gravemother case. A qualified signal only

422:   qualifiable?: QualifierKind;

425: function matches(matcher: Matcher, facts: CardFacts): boolean {
426:   return typeof matcher === 'function' ? matcher(facts) : matcher.test(facts.text);

632: /** Splits text into clauses, so a qualifier is only picked up from the same
633:  * sentence as the payoff it restricts. */
634: function clauses(text: string): string[] {
635:   return text.split(/[.;\n]/).filter((c) => c.trim().length > 0);
636: }
637: 
638: /**
639:  * The creature type a qualifiable archetype's payoff is restricted to, if any.
640:  *
641:  * Only a type mentioned in the same clause as the payoff counts ΓÇö a commander
642:  * that reanimates anything and separately happens to mention Goblins is not a
643:  * Goblin-restricted reanimator.
644:  */
645: function findQualifier(facts: CardFacts, def: ArchetypeDef, vocab: Vocabulary): string | undefined {
646:   const payoffMatchers = [...(def.roles.rewards ?? []), ...(def.roles.consumes ?? [])];
647:   for (const clause of clauses(facts.text)) {
648:     const hit = payoffMatchers.some((m) => (typeof m === 'function' ? false : m.test(clause)));
649:     if (!hit) continue;
650:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
651:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
652:       if (type) return type;
653:     }
654:   }
655:   return undefined;
656: }
657: 
658: function rolesFor(def: ArchetypeDef, facts: CardFacts): Role[] {
659:   const found: Role[] = [];
660:   for (const role of ROLES) {
661:     const matchers = def.roles[role];
662:     if (matchers?.some((m) => matches(m, facts))) found.push(role);
663:   }
664:   return found;
665: }
666: 
667: /**
668:  * The creature types a card could possibly relate to.
669:  *
670:  * Derived from the card outward rather than by testing every type in the
671:  * game against it. That is not just an optimisation: looping the full
672:  * vocabulary meant 647 types x 884 keywords of regex per card, which took
673:  * 82 seconds across the card pool and made precomputing signals impractical.
674:  * Scanning the card's own words and intersecting with the known-type set is
675:  * proportional to the card, not to Magic's type list.
676:  */
677: function candidateTypes(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
678:   const found = new Set<string>();
679:   // Structured, and free.
680:   for (const type of facts.creatureTypes) found.add(type);
681:   for (const type of facts.producedTokenTypes) found.add(type);
682:   // Textual: every word the card uses, looked up rather than searched for.
683:   for (const word of wordsIn(facts.text)) {
684:     const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
685:     if (type) found.add(type);
686:   }
687:   return [...found];
688: }
689: 
690: /** Kindred, one signal per creature type. Membership is structural (the card's
691:  * own type, or a token type it makes); caring about the type is textual. */
692: function detectKindred(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): SignalMatch[] {
693:   const out: SignalMatch[] = [];
694:   for (const type of candidateTypes(facts, vocab)) {
695:     const roles: Role[] = [];
696:     // Structured data only ΓÇö never the name. Goblin Sharpshooter is a Goblin
697:     // because its type line says so.
698:     if (facts.creatureTypes.includes(type)) roles.push('is');
699:     // "Create two 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens" makes Krenko's Command a
700:     // Goblin card even though a Sorcery has no creature type.
701:     if (facts.producedTokenTypes.includes(type)) roles.push('produces');
702: 
703:     // Naming the token's type is not caring about the type ΓÇö "create two 1/1
704:     // red Goblin creature tokens" already counted as `produces` above, and
705:     // must not also read as a payoff. Krenko's Command says "Goblin" exactly
706:     // once, in the token's name, and is a producer only; Krenko, Mob Boss
707:     // says it twice ΓÇö once naming the token, once counting "the number of
708:     // Goblins you control" ΓÇö and that second mention is the payoff.
709:     const caringText = facts.text.replace(tokenDescriptorPattern(type), ' ');
710: 
711:     for (const clause of clauses(caringText)) {
712:       if (!wordPattern(type).test(clause)) continue;
713:       const consumesType = /\bsacrifice\b|\btap\b|\bdiscard\b|\bexile\b/i.test(clause);
714:       if (consumesType) {
715:         roles.push('consumes');
716:         // An activated ability is "cost: effect", so a clause that spends the
717:         // type also hands something back. Lathril's "Tap ten untapped Elves
718:         // you control: Each opponent loses 10 life" consumes Elves *and*
719:         // rewards you for having had them.
720:         if (clause.includes(':')) roles.push('rewards');
721:       }
722:       if (
723:         /\bget\b|\bgains?\b|\bhas\b|\bhave\b|whenever|for each|number of|search|\blose\b|\bloses\b/i.test(
724:           clause,
725:         )
726:       ) {
727:         roles.push('rewards');
728:       }
729:       // Mentioned outside a token's name, in a way none of the above caught ΓÇö
730:       // still active interest in the type, which is what separates Krenko
731:       // from Silas Renn.
732:       if (!consumesType && !roles.includes('rewards')) roles.push('rewards');
733:     }
734: 
735:     if (roles.length === 0) continue;
736:     out.push({
737:       archetype: 'kindred',
738:       label: `${type} Kindred`,
739:       description: `${pluralOfType(type)}, and cards that care about having them.`,
740:       weight: 15,
741:       qualifier: type,
742:       qualifierKind: 'creatureType',
743:       roles: [...new Set(roles)],
744:     });
745:   }
746:   return out;
747: }
748: 
749: /**
750:  * Keyword care, one signal per keyword.
751:  *
752:  * A keyword on its own is not a synergy ΓÇö Trample is a good thing to have,
753:  * not a deck. What matters is a commander that *cares* about the keyword
754:  * (grants it, or triggers off it), which is the same active-role test kindred
755:  * uses. Having the keyword is `is` and never qualifies a commander on its own.
756:  */
757: function detectKeywordCare(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): SignalMatch[] {
758:   const out: SignalMatch[] = [];
759:   for (const keyword of candidateKeywords(facts, vocab)) {
760:     if (EXCLUDED_KEYWORDS.has(keyword.toLowerCase())) continue;
761:     const roles: Role[] = [];
762:     if (facts.keywords.includes(keyword)) roles.push('is');
763:     const pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${escapeRegExp(keyword)}\\b`, 'i');
764:     for (const clause of clauses(facts.text)) {
765:       if (!pattern.test(clause)) continue;
766:       // "Creatures you control gain trample" / "have flying" ΓÇö granting it to
767:       // others, which is the Craterhoof shape.
768:       if (/\b(?:gains?|have|has|gets?)\b/i.test(clause)) roles.push('produces');
769:       if (/whenever|for each|number of/i.test(clause)) roles.push('rewards');
770:     }
771:     if (roles.length === 0) continue;
772:     out.push({
773:       archetype: 'keywordCare',
774:       label: keyword,
775:       description: `Cards with ${keyword}, where the commander actually cares about it.`,
776:       weight: 8,
777:       qualifier: keyword,
778:       qualifierKind: 'keyword',
779:       roles: [...new Set(roles)],
780:     });
781:   }
782:   return out;
783: }
784: 
785: /**
786:  * Keywords that are structural rather than thematic.
787:  *
788:  * The Partner family says who can be your commander, not what your deck
789:  * wants to do. Surfacing "Partner" as a shared keyword would be a confusing
790:  * echo of the dedicated partner/background handling rather than a second,
791:  * unrelated signal.
792:  */
793: const EXCLUDED_KEYWORDS = new Set([
794:   'partner',
795:   'partner with',
796:   'friends forever',
797:   'choose a background',
798:   "doctor's companion",
799: ]);
800: 
801: /** The keywords a card could possibly relate to. Same inversion as
802:  * `candidateTypes` ΓÇö look up the card's own words instead of testing all 884
803:  * keywords against it. Multi-word keywords ("first strike") can't be found by
804:  * single-word lookup, so those few are still tested directly. */
805: function candidateKeywords(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
806:   const found = new Set<string>();
807:   for (const keyword of facts.keywords) found.add(keyword);
808:   for (const word of wordsIn(facts.text)) {
809:     const keyword = vocab.keywordByWord.get(word);
810:     if (keyword) found.add(keyword);
811:   }
812:   const lowerText = facts.text.toLowerCase();
813:   for (const keyword of vocab.multiWordKeywords) {
814:     if (lowerText.includes(keyword.toLowerCase())) found.add(keyword);
815:   }
816:   return [...found];
817: }
818: 
819: /** Every archetype this card participates in, and how. */
820: export function detectSignals(facts: CardFacts, vocab: Vocabulary): SignalMatch[] {
821:   const out: SignalMatch[] = [];
822: 
823:   for (const def of ARCHETYPES) {
824:     const roles = rolesFor(def, facts);
825:     if (roles.length === 0) continue;
826:     const qualifier = def.qualifiable ? findQualifier(facts, def, vocab) : undefined;
827:     out.push({
828:       archetype: def.key,
829:       label: qualifier ? `${def.label} (${qualifier})` : def.label,
830:       description: def.description,
831:       weight: def.weight,
832:       qualifier,
833:       qualifierKind: qualifier ? def.qualifiable : undefined,
834:       roles,
835:     });
836:   }
837: 
838:   out.push(...detectKindred(facts, vocab));
839:   out.push(...detectKeywordCare(facts, vocab));
840:   return out;
841: }
842: 
843: /**
844:  * Whether a card in the list can support a signal the commander showed.
845:  *
846:  * Unqualified signals accept any card that participates in the archetype at
847:  * all. A *qualified* signal additionally requires the supporter to be of that
848:  * subtype ΓÇö this is the Sliver Gravemother rule, and it is the whole reason
849:  * qualifiers exist.
850:  */
851: export function supports(signal: SignalMatch, supporter: SignalMatch[], facts: CardFacts): boolean {
852:   const sameArchetype = supporter.filter((s) => s.archetype === signal.archetype);
853:   if (sameArchetype.length === 0) return false;
854:   if (!signal.qualifier) return true;
855: 
856:   if (signal.qualifierKind === 'creatureType') {
857:     return (
858:       facts.creatureTypes.includes(signal.qualifier) ||
859:       facts.producedTokenTypes.includes(signal.qualifier)
860:     );
861:   }
862:   if (signal.qualifierKind === 'keyword') {
863:     return facts.keywords.includes(signal.qualifier);
864:   }
865:   return sameArchetype.some((s) => s.qualifier === signal.qualifier);
866: }
867: 
868: /**
869:  * Presentation details for a signal read back out of storage.
870:  *
871:  * The `card_signals` table records what a card *is* ΓÇö archetype, qualifier,
872:  * roles ΓÇö and deliberately not how to label it. Labels and weights are
873:  * presentation, and storing them would mean a reworded description needed a
874:  * full re-import to take effect. This rebuilds them from the catalog instead.
875:  */
876: export function archetypeDisplay(
877:   archetype: string,
878:   qualifier: string | null,
879: ): { label: string; description: string; weight: number } {
880:   if (archetype === 'kindred' && qualifier) {
881:     return {
882:       label: `${qualifier} Kindred`,
883:       description: `${pluralOfType(qualifier)}, and cards that care about having them.`,
884:       weight: 15,
885:     };
886:   }
887:   if (archetype === 'keywordCare' && qualifier) {
888:     return {
889:       label: qualifier,
890:       description: `Cards with ${qualifier}, where the commander actually cares about it.`,
891:       weight: 8,
892:     };
893:   }
894: 
895:   const def = ARCHETYPES.find((a) => a.key === archetype);
896:   if (!def) {
897:     // An archetype in the database that the catalog no longer defines ΓÇö the
898:     // shape of things after a rename without a re-import. Degrade to the raw
899:     // key rather than crashing; the next import drops the row.
900:     return { label: archetype, description: '', weight: 10 };
901:   }
902:   return {
903:     label: qualifier ? `${def.label} (${qualifier})` : def.label,
904:     description: def.description,
905:     weight: def.weight,
906:   };
907: }

(End of file - total 907 lines)

# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code when working in `apps/commander-recommender/`.

## What this is

A Commander recommender: paste or upload a card list, get ranked Commander suggestions ΓÇö
including Partner/Background pairs ΓÇö with cited synergies, ban-list legality, and an estimated
Bracket. React 19 + Vite client (Zustand + TanStack Query/Table), Express 5 + better-sqlite3
server, no ORM. Card data is Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk export, imported into SQLite at
build/deploy time ΓÇö the running server never calls Scryfall live.

Read [`../../docs/commander-recommender.md`](../../docs/commander-recommender.md) first ΓÇö it's
this app's own handoff document (moved here during the monorepo consolidation, file map kept
current) and covers the deeper "why" behind the stack choices, the scoring model, and known risk
areas in more depth than this file repeats. This file is about how to work in the code, not what
the code does. The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md) covers workspace-wide commands and
conventions this file doesn't repeat.

## Commands

Run from `apps/commander-recommender/` unless noted (or use `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client`
/ `--filter mtg-recommender-server` from the repo root).

- `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-client dev` and `pnpm --filter mtg-recommender-server dev`, or
  both via `pnpm dev` from the repo root ΓÇö API on `:4000`, Vite client on `:5173` (proxies `/api`)
- `cd server && pnpm run prepare-data` ΓÇö downloads Scryfall's Oracle Cards bulk file and seeds
  `server/data/cards.sqlite`; required before `/api/recommend` returns anything but a 503. Needs
  network access; reuses a copy less than a week old unless run as `prepare-data:fresh`
- `cd server && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`,
  `src/` only, test files excluded ΓÇö see the note in `tsconfig.build.json` about why `rootDir`
  matters here) / `pnpm test` (Vitest, 12 files colocated under `src/services/`)
- `cd client && pnpm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`) / `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) /
  `pnpm test` (Vitest, 5 files colocated under `src/lib/`)
- `pnpm run lint` in either ΓÇö no type-aware rules (see `packages/config/eslint.base.js`)
- Single test file: `pnpm exec vitest run src/services/synergy.test.ts` (or any other), from
  whichever of `client`/`server` it lives in

## Architecture

- **`server/src/services/synergy.ts`** is the heart of the app: builds a `CollectionProfile` from
  the matched cards (color identity, creature types, keywords, oracle-text theme regexes), then
  scores every `CommanderUnit` from `partners.ts` against it. A signal counts only once it clears
  `MIN_SIGNAL_COUNT` (3) distinct supporting cards _after_ narrowing to that unit's color identity.
  Kindred requires the unit's own text to _care_ about a type (`caresAboutCreatureType`), not
  merely have it. Color identity gates eligibility and contributes nothing to score ΓÇö see the
  "scoring measures focus" tests in `synergy.test.ts` before changing the weight formula.
- **`server/src/services/signals.ts`** (879 lines, the largest file) is the signal/role model
  feeding `synergy.ts`: what a card contributes to a deck's plan (`is`/`produces`/`consumes`/
  `rewards`/`amplifies`) and in what capacity. `deckAnalysis.ts` + `lifecycle.ts` + `packages.ts`
  build on it to answer "what is this list trying to do, and what's it missing" independent of any
  commander ΓÇö see `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map for how those three fit together.
- **`server/src/services/partners.ts`** builds every legal `CommanderUnit` (rule 702.124: one card
  or a legal pair) from the eligible pool ΓÇö a `CommanderUnit` is what `synergy.ts` scores, not a
  bare `CardRow`. Grouped by ability variant (Partner, PartnerΓÇö[text], Partner with [Name], Friends
  forever, Choose a Background, Doctor's companion) rather than a cross-product.
- **`server/src/services/eligibility.ts`** judges commander eligibility on a card's **front face
  only** (CR 712.4) ΓÇö Scryfall's top-level `type_line` for a DFC is both faces joined, which is why
  this can't just substring-match the whole thing. `split` is the deliberate exception (CR 709.4).
  This runs at import time (`import-scryfall.ts`'s only caller), so a stale `cards.sqlite` keeps
  old eligibility until re-imported.
- **`server/src/db.ts`** ΓÇö SQLite connection + `isSeeded` guard (returns 503 instead of a raw SQL
  error pre-import) + `findCardsByNames`, which falls back to a `card_face_names` table (built by
  `cardNames.ts`'s rules) so a decklist naming only one face of a DFC still resolves.
- **`server/scripts/fetch-scryfall.ts`** + **`import-scryfall.ts`** are the only place Scryfall is
  called from this app ΓÇö see [`../../docs/api-policy.md`](../../docs/api-policy.md), a hard
  project rule, before changing what these call or when.
- **`server/src/services/spellbook.ts`** ΓÇö Commander Spellbook adapter. Click-triggered only, 1-hour
  in-memory cache, no retry on 429. Same hard-rule constraints apply.
- **Cited-card dedup**: the server sends each cited card once (`server/src/services/cardIndex.ts`)
  and cites it by position; `client/src/lib/rehydrate.ts` puts cards back together at the API
  boundary. This is why a 12MB response became 0.25MB (see `CHANGELOG.md` 1.7.1) ΓÇö don't bypass it
  by threading whole card objects through a new code path.
- **`client/src/api/`** ΓÇö `client.ts` (fetch + cold-start retry against Render's free-tier sleep)
  wrapped by `queries.ts` (TanStack Query hooks). The `retry`/`refetchOnWindowFocus`/
  `refetchOnReconnect: false` defaults in `main.tsx` are load-bearing against Commander
  Spellbook traffic ΓÇö don't restore them without re-reading the api-policy doc.
- **`client/src/store/`** splits by what the state _is_: `useAppStore` (not persisted ΓÇö textarea
  contents, submitted list, dismissals) vs. `usePreferencesStore` (persisted to `localStorage` ΓÇö
  durable UI prefs like page size). Don't merge these; a dismissal surviving a browser restart
  against a different pasted list would be surprising, but a page-size choice should outlive the
  tab.
- **`client/src/lib/mtg.ts`** ΓÇö WUBRG ordering and color-identity naming ("Golgari", never
  "Black/Green"). **`client/src/lib/manaSymbols.ts`** ΓÇö inlined SVG mana glyph paths (see
  `docs/rules-audit.md` item 16 ΓÇö this file is a Phase 2 migration target for `@mtg/mana`).
- A suggestion is a `CommanderUnit` (1-2 `CardRow`s), not a single card ΓÇö every DTO, filter, and
  sort in the client threads through that union, not a flattened card.

## Conventions

- Comments explain _why_, not _what_ ΓÇö match the existing tone (see `synergy.ts`'s comments on the
  scoring formula, or `eligibility.ts`'s on front-face-only reasoning).
- Keep changes proportional to the ask. This codebase deliberately favors a short, readable
  heuristic over a "complete" system in synergy detection and Bracket estimation ΓÇö see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Core logic" section before making one more sophisticated.
- Match the existing pattern for whichever file you're touching. If the surrounding code uses a
  plain function and a `Set`, don't reach for a class or a new dependency to do the same job.
- **Never write oracle text from memory ΓÇö copy it from the database.** Scryfall has moved much
  self-referential wording from a card's name to "this creature"/"this land"; two rules in this
  codebase were written from recall and were wrong on real cards (see
  `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s "Known risk areas"). Every string in `signals.test.ts` is
  copied verbatim from the imported database ΓÇö keep it that way.
- Before opening a PR: typecheck and test both `client/` and `server/`, and actually run the app
  for anything user-visible ΓÇö a clean typecheck and passing tests are necessary, not sufficient
  (they don't catch a CSS rule that silently stopped applying, for instance).
- Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]` for any user-facing change, in the existing
  style (see `1.7.1`'s entry for the level of detail expected).
- `docs/commander-recommender.md`'s file map is meant to stay current ΓÇö update it in the same
  commit whenever you add, rename, or remove a file it lists.

/**
 * The signal model: what a card contributes to a deck's plan, and in what
 * capacity.
 *
 * This replaces the old flat "theme" model, in which a signal was a single
 * regex applied identically to your card and to the candidate commander, and
 * two cards "synergised" when the same words appeared in both. That measured
 * lexical co-occurrence rather than synergy: "Sacrifice a creature" and
 * "Sacrifice Arid Mesa" are the same word and completely different mechanics,
 * and a commander that pays off a plan (Craterhoof Behemoth pumping your
 * board) usually shares no vocabulary at all with the cards that set it up.
 *
 * Three ideas do the work here.
 *
 * 1. ROLES. A card doesn't just "have" a theme, it participates in one in a
 *    particular capacity ΓÇö see `Role`. This is what lets one card carry
 *    several unrelated signals: Goblin Sharpshooter is Goblin kindred because
 *    of its creature *type*, and part of the creature-death cluster because of
 *    its *text*, and those two facts have nothing to do with each other.
 *

 * Tests for the signal/role model.
 *
 * Every oracle text below is copied verbatim from the imported Scryfall
 * database, not written from memory. That matters more than it sounds:
