 * name to "this creature" / "this land", so text recalled from older printings
 * exercises patterns that no longer occur. Re-copy from the database rather
 * than hand-editing these strings.
 */
import assert from 'node:assert';
import { describe, it } from 'vitest';
import type { CardRow } from '../types';
import {
  buildCardFacts,
  buildVocabulary,
  detectSignals,
  hasActiveRole,

<content>
1: import type { CardRow } from '../types';
2: 
3: /**
4:  * A commander as actually played: one card, or two under a Partner-family
5:  * ability (702.124). Every card in `cards` is jointly "the commander" ΓÇö
6:  * there's no primary/secondary in the rules (702.124e), so this is an array
7:  * rather than a "main card + optional partner" shape.
8:  */
9: export interface CommanderUnit {
10:   cards: CardRow[];
11: }
12: 
13: function parseJsonArray(value: string | null): string[] {
14:   if (!value) return [];
15:   try {
16:     const parsed = JSON.parse(value);
17:     return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [];
18:   } catch {
19:     return [];
20:   }
21: }
22: 
23: function creatureTypeSet(card: CardRow): Set<string> {
24:   return new Set(parseJsonArray(card.creature_types));
25: }
26: 
27: function setEquals(a: Set<string>, b: Set<string>): boolean {
28:   return a.size === b.size && [...a].every((item) => b.has(item));
29: }
30: 
31: /** Stable id for a unit, used to dedupe pairs regardless of which card was found first. */
32: export function unitKey(unit: CommanderUnit): string {
33:   return unit.cards
34:     .map((c) => c.oracle_id)
35:     .sort()
36:     .join('+');
37: }
38: 
39: /**
40:  * Builds every legal "commander unit" from the eligible candidate pool: one
41:  * per solo card, plus one per valid Partner/Partner-with/PartnerΓÇösuffix/
42:  * Friends-forever/Choose-a-Background/Doctor's-companion pair.
43:  *
44:  * Pairing is grouped by ability variant rather than a blind cross-product
45:  * over every candidate ΓÇö with an eligible pool in the tens to low hundreds,
46:  * pairing only within (or against) the relevant sub-groups keeps this cheap
47:  * enough to run per request, which is what was asked for. Different partner
48:  * variants never combine with each other (702.124f) ΓÇö a plain-Partner card
49:  * cannot pair with a Partner-with card, for instance ΓÇö which pairing only
50:  * within each group already guarantees.
51:  *
52:  * A card with a partner ability still gets its own solo unit too: every
53:  * variant here is optional (903.3 / 702.124a), so a Partner card is a
54:  * perfectly legal commander by itself. The one exception is Background
55:  * enchantments, which never appear as a solo candidate in the first place
56:  * (they're not a creature/Vehicle/Spacecraft, so getCommanderCandidates
57:  * already excludes them) and are only ever reached here as a pairing target.
58:  */
59: export function buildCommanderUnits(
60:   candidates: CardRow[],
61:   backgrounds: CardRow[],
62: ): CommanderUnit[] {
63:   const units: CommanderUnit[] = candidates.map((card) => ({ cards: [card] }));
64:   const seenPairs = new Set<string>();
65: 
66:   function addPair(a: CardRow, b: CardRow): void {
67:     if (a.oracle_id === b.oracle_id) return;
68:     const key = [a.oracle_id, b.oracle_id].sort().join('+');
69:     if (seenPairs.has(key)) return;
70:     seenPairs.add(key);
71:     units.push({ cards: [a, b] });
72:   }
73: 
74:   function pairAllWithin(group: CardRow[]): void {
75:     for (let i = 0; i < group.length; i++) {
76:       // Both i and j are always within [0, group.length) by the loop bounds.
77:       for (let j = i + 1; j < group.length; j++) addPair(group[i]!, group[j]!);
78:     }
79:   }
80: 
81:   const byAbility = (ability: CardRow['partner_ability']) =>
82:     candidates.filter((c) => c.partner_ability === ability);
83: 
84:   // Plain Partner: any two.
85:   pairAllWithin(byAbility('partner'));
86: 
87:   // PartnerΓÇö[text]: only within the same suffix group.
88:   const suffixGroups = new Map<string, CardRow[]>();
89:   for (const card of byAbility('partner_suffix')) {
90:     const key = card.partner_target ?? '';
91:     const group = suffixGroups.get(key);
92:     if (group) group.push(card);
93:     else suffixGroups.set(key, [card]);
94:   }
95:   for (const group of suffixGroups.values()) pairAllWithin(group);
96: 
97:   // Partner with [Name]: symmetric named pairing ΓÇö each card must name the
98:   // other (702.124j), not just be named by it.
99:   const byNameLower = new Map(candidates.map((c) => [c.name_lower, c]));
100:   for (const card of byAbility('partner_with')) {
101:     const target = card.partner_target ? byNameLower.get(card.partner_target) : undefined;
102:     if (target?.partner_ability === 'partner_with' && target.partner_target === card.name_lower) {
103:       addPair(card, target);
104:     }
105:   }
106: 
107:   // Friends forever: any two. Restricted to creatures by the rule (702.124k),
108:   // which every real friends-forever card already satisfies as printed ΓÇö
109:   // checked anyway rather than assumed, since nothing stops a future card
110:   // from breaking that pattern.
111:   pairAllWithin(
112:     byAbility('friends_forever').filter((c) => (c.type_line ?? '').includes('Creature')),
113:   );
114: 
115:   // Choose a Background: the companion card ├ù every legal legendary Background.
116:   for (const chooser of byAbility('choose_background')) {
117:     for (const background of backgrounds) addPair(chooser, background);
118:   }
119: 
120:   // Doctor's companion: the companion card ├ù any legendary creature whose
121:   // creature types are *exactly* Time Lord and Doctor ΓÇö no other subtypes.
122:   const timeLordDoctor = new Set(['Time Lord', 'Doctor']);
123:   const doctors = candidates.filter((c) => setEquals(creatureTypeSet(c), timeLordDoctor));
124:   for (const companion of byAbility('doctors_companion')) {
125:     for (const doctor of doctors) addPair(companion, doctor);
126:   }
127: 
128:   return units;
129: }
